reason: CPMP supplied evidence of Gemma L4x4 access; correct misleading exclusivity inference

changes.before: He pointed at the L4s early. ARC-2 runs on Kaggle’s L4x4 machines, four NVIDIA L4 chips apiece, and Kaggle’s own page calls them limited, which makes NVIDIA’s own chips the scarce thing this weekend. changes.after:
He pointed at the L4s early. ARC-2 runs on Kaggle’s L4x4 machines, four NVIDIA L4 chips apiece, and Kaggle’s own page calls that access limited. A month ago CPMP warned Kaggle staff the L4 queue was jammed, and Kaggle’s Dustin answered that demand had increased considerably and added capacity. Gemma’s competition page explicitly offers Kaggle L4x4 machines. CPMP pointed this out in his November 1 reply to our article, and he was right: our earlier wording gave the misleading impression that the hardware was exclusive to ARC-2. Both competitions offer that hardware.

Gemma’s discussion board supplies further evidence. On September 28, Ryan Holbrook paused rescoring because of L4x4 queues. On October 8, Dustin attributed long waits and erroneous failures to heavy L4 submission volume; Holbrook said the next day that doubling the machines had not contained demand. Dustin put the queue at about 33 hours on October 10. ARC-2 staff separately acknowledged more sessions than machines. These overlapping reports support CPMP’s contention that the contests faced pressure on Kaggle’s L4 capacity; the share of ARC delays attributable specifically to Gemma is not established.

Correction · November 1, 2026: We have corrected the implication that L4x4 access was exclusive to ARC-2. Thanks to CPMP’s reply; see Gemma’s Upgraded Accelerators section. We have also added Kaggle staff’s documented L4 capacity and queue problems in both competitions.
